review_method: Read every supplied complete record: titles, chapters, captions/context, all parts and body rows, footnotes, transcription notes and English layer where present. Compared against approved definitions and relevant includes/excludes. No OCR, external model calls or source edits.

candidates.label: census and survey methods
candidates.definition: The organisation, instruments and procedures used to collect census or survey information.
includes: Census questions, blank survey cards, schedules and enumeration forms.
Instructions to enumerators, census-board reporting categories and data-collection procedures.
excludes: Ordinary population, religious or household statistics merely derived from a census or survey.
Legal household registration without a census or survey collection subject.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: household-registration is legal registration rather than enumeration methodology. The subject tags for requested answers do not describe the blank instrument itself, and scientific-research would infer a research activity not established by every census form.

candidates.label: distances and journey times
candidates.definition: Measured distances or elapsed travelling times between places along routes, or in comparative origin-destination tables.
includes: Sea, river, rail and overland distance matrices.
Route lengths and comparative journey durations from a place to other destinations.
excludes: Calendar dates, clock-time conversions and time-zone tables.
Ticket fares and freight charges without route-distance or duration measures.
A railway inventory whose principal subject is railway operation rather than comparative access between places.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: shipping, inland-navigation or railways can already describe many explicitly identified modes; those existing fits are separately recorded. None names the common distance/time measure across mixed modes, and generic overland or place-to-place distances should not require an inferred transport mode. rivers-and-waterways concerns physical river regimes, while freight-and-transport-costs concerns money, not miles.

candidates.label: real estate
candidates.definition: Transactions, market values and rents of land and buildings as property.
includes: Land and building sales, transaction areas and consideration paid.
Urban land lease rents and quoted values or rents of offices, warehouses and residential property.
excludes: Agricultural ownership and tenancy arrangements without a property-market measure: use land-tenure.
Property taxation alone: use land-tax or taxation.
Residential overcrowding, dwelling conditions or housing support without a property-market subject: use housing.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: land-tenure is explicitly agricultural. housing covers dwellings but not the combined office, warehouse and land-market schedules; land-tax would confuse rent with tax. prices is a possible general quotation fallback, but its defined examples concern goods/services and it does not identify real-property transactions.

candidates.label: commodity origins
candidates.definition: The geographical distribution of the origins or producing regions of commodities, especially comparative inventories across products or sectors.
includes: Product-to-province and province-to-product origin catalogues.
Producing districts linked to export ports or outward routes as an explicitly organised geographical inventory.
excludes: A numerical crop, mine or factory production table merely broken down by province.
General economic indicators combining quantitative domains.
A single incidental place name in a commodity table.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: The catalogues span agriculture, animal products, forestry, mining and manufactures. crop-production, mineral-production and industrial-output each omit major sectors, while economic-indicators requires a general economic barometer rather than a qualitative origin catalogue. exports already fits the outward-port catalogues but does not describe their origin mapping.

candidates.label: printing
candidates.definition: Printing, lithography, engraving and related reproduction of printed matter, including the establishments providing these services.
includes: Printing and lithographic works, presses and engraving establishments.
Printing capacity, production, personnel, charges and business inventories.
excludes: Paper and pulp production without printing.
Lists or circulation of publications without a printing-production or printing-establishment subject.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: books, newspapers and periodicals classify publication types, not a cross-publication printing industry; paper-and-pulp concerns the material. companies or industrial-output are usable generic fallbacks, but neither identifies this distinct productive activity.

candidates.label: fish and fish products
candidates.definition: Fish and primary or processed fish commodities in commerce, supply and processing when capture or cultivation is not the principal stated activity.
includes: Trade, market supply and commodity values of fish and fishery products.
Fresh, dried, salted and otherwise processed fish products, when the source identifies them.
excludes: Catch, fishing fleets and capture operations: use fishing.
Aquaculture operations alone: use aquaculture.
Whaling and seaweed when their dedicated tags suffice.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: The source gives customs movement values of fish and fishery products, without stating import/export direction or capture/cultivation origin. fishing is defined around capture operations and aquaculture would invent an origin; food-processing would assume all the trade concerns processed products.

candidates.label: domestic service
candidates.definition: Paid or otherwise dependent household service performed by servants and the households employing them.
includes: Domestic servants, household employers, servant wages and conditions.
Counts and proportions of households keeping servants.
excludes: Household manufacture: use cottage-industries.
Public service employment or workers serving customers outside private households.
Family composition or budgets without a domestic-service subject.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: The table counts families employing servants, not servant workers, occupations, hours or remuneration. households is demographic rather than a household labour arrangement; employment-and-unemployment or working-conditions would be only approximate. The subject is useful beyond this one social-survey cross-tabulation.

candidates.label: native-place associations
candidates.definition: Associations and collective institutions organised around a shared town, district or provincial place of origin.
includes: Native-place guilds, provincial associations and huiguan halls.
Their membership, facilities, accommodation, mutual support and finances.
excludes: Merchant or industrial associations organised primarily by business or occupation: use business-associations.
An overseas population count without a native-place association as subject.
Ordinary hotel or dwelling inventories without a native-place institution.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: The source counts halls built by cities/districts of each province, not occupational merchant guilds. overseas-communities is defined by national or ethnic origin and would not reliably describe domestic provincial associations. housing is a service-level fallback given the contextual accommodation function, but misses the institutional basis.

candidates.label: foreign trade
candidates.definition: Merchandise exchange across a territory's external trade boundary when treated in aggregate or without a supported single direction.
includes: Combined total imports-and-exports values by port, partner or period.
Explicit foreign-country merchandise trade for which the source does not establish import/export direction.
excludes: Domestic exchange and purely internal customs movements without external-trade evidence.
Cross-border service, income and capital accounts: use the relevant balance-of-payments or services tags.
A direction-specific series adequately described by imports or exports.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: imports and exports describe separate directions, not an undivided total. Most other examples here also have missing commodity labels or conflicting continuation context, so their uncertainty is a source-quality issue as well as a vocabulary gap. A broad foreign-trade tag is justified by the clean aggregate port table, but must not be presented as repairing the damaged detailed identification.

candidates.label: school curricula
candidates.definition: Prescribed subjects, courses, lesson hours and credits that organise formal school instruction.
includes: Weekly timetables, course-hour allocations, curriculum requirements and academic credits.
Comparisons of prescribed instruction by grade or school type.
excludes: Enrolment or school counts without instructional content.
Subjects of public lectures without a formal school curriculum.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: primary-education already fits and should not have been left empty. This is an optional narrower discovery term across school stages, not evidence that the current vocabulary cannot classify the table.

candidates.label: demobilisation
candidates.definition: The disbandment, reduction or release of armed forces and the organisation or financing of that process.
includes: Troop-disbandment allocations and implementation.
Release and transition measures explicitly tied to military demobilisation.
excludes: Recruitment or mobilisation.
Veterans' continuing benefits or employment when the demobilisation process itself is not the subject.
Routine peacetime force organisation.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: army and public-budgets already fit this disbandment funding table. The optional term would distinguish reduction/release from war-and-mobilisation and from routine army accounts; it is not necessary simply to eliminate an empty tag list.

deferred.reason: The source gives court-style titles of a professional storytellers' guild, but not enough about whether it coordinates businesses, represents workers or serves as a mutual society. Do not infer government offices from the theatrical office titles. A general occupational-guilds addition should wait for clearer recurring evidence; business-associations may fit after contextual confirmation.

A proposed translation-source author list for the New Thought Movement is clear, but one list of thinkers is insufficient reason to add a broad intellectual-movements or philosophy category. It does not list book titles or formal curricula. Retain for wider-corpus evaluation.

The office/count schedule of the Lu Pan Industrial Union does not establish whether it represents workers or commercial establishments. The name alone cannot resolve trade-unions versus business-associations; do not create a guild/union synonym merely to avoid this source ambiguity.

Association names and addresses do not establish whether the foreign organisations are business lobbies, community support bodies or diplomatic organisations. Do not infer their purpose from known historical names without supplied evidence; seek adjacent context before proposing a special foreign-associations tag.

The single list of dates of first trade contacts is a narrow commercial chronology. historical-chronologies explicitly excludes a single-subject chronology adequately described by its subject, and a separate trade-history tag would be weakly evidenced here. Retain pending wider demand for commercial-relations history.

The supplied title calls these land transactions, but the transcription notes explicitly say the lead-in establishing what the area/cost figures refer to was not read. real-estate is a plausible candidate; confirm the transaction context before assigning it.
